output.summary: The yield decline is real: inspection, gauges and reject criteria are unchanged (E4). The 12-hour switch is not a proven cause. The decline began in week 32, before the 10 August shift change, the scrap-tag timing is a recording artifact (E3), and new operators reject at the same rate as experienced ones (E14). The deferred spindle service is the best-supported driver: runout is above limit on L3-02 and L3-05 and vibration is rising (E10), though the rise across all six lathes and the tighter long-shaft tolerance confound it (E11). Corvane spread shows only association, and the decline occurred on low-spread bar. Do not present the 8-hour return as the root-cause fix, do not discipline new operators, and do not cut CMM sampling. Complete the spindle service in staggered groups with logged data and Tamsworth trials. Evidence is insufficient to commit to a substantive fix yet.
